questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to make good coffee at home without an expensive machine
Why coffee is bad for our health if we drink too much
How cafés changed from places of debate to places to work alone
The best cafés in Oxford and London and what makes them special
questions.why: They compare early coffee houses, full of lively debate, with modern cafés where people sit on laptops.

questions.q: Why did Catherine take so long to bring Rob's coffee?
options: She met someone she knew and stopped to talk
The café was very busy
She had to wait for the wifi
She forgot how Rob likes his coffee
questions.why: She says she bumped into somebody she knew in the café and stopped for a chat.

questions.q: Where and when was the first coffee house opened?
options: In London in 1560
In Edinburgh in 1650
In London in 1750
In Oxford in 1650
questions.why: Rob says the first coffee house was set up in Oxford in 1650.

questions.q: What did a penny buy you in the early coffee houses?
options: A cup of coffee and a cake
Entry, newspapers and interesting conversation
A comfortable chair for the whole day
A place in a debating competition
questions.why: You paid a penny to get in, which included access to newspapers and stimulating conversation.

questions.q: What did Catherine notice in the café that morning?
options: It was full of people debating
The coffee had become more expensive
Many people were reading newspapers
Only she and her friend were talking
questions.why: She says nobody else was talking; everybody sat alone tapping on their laptops.

questions.q: How does Douglas Fraser describe a typical modern café?
options: People sit alone, looking at screens, doing different things
People share large tables and work together on projects
It is empty until lunchtime, when office workers arrive
People chat loudly about the news and politics of the day
questions.why: He describes five people staring into screens, 'plugged in, ears plugged', each doing something different.

questions.q: What does Rob think café owners should do?
options: Add more comfortable sofas
Switch off the free wifi so people move on
Offer free coffee to people who talk
Bring back the penny entry fee
questions.why: Rob says owners should turn off the free wifi and force the 'café squatters' to move on.

questions.q: How does Catherine respond to Rob's idea?
options: She agrees completely and says she would do the same
She says most people do buy coffee, so it isn't needed
She thinks it's too extreme, as cafés want people to stay
She says wifi is too expensive for most small cafés
questions.why: She calls it 'a bit extreme' because café owners need customers and encourage them to stay.
